column2: keepers of Shiva's command, worthy of my worship too by Shiva's teaching — may all favour me and proclaim my rite fruitful.
Those devoted to the southern knowledge and those who walk the southern and northern paths — may they abide without opposition to my mantra, seeking my welfare.
Unbelievers, deceivers, the ungrateful, the tamasic, heretics and great sinners — may they stay far from me.
What need of praising many here? Whoever are believers, all of them, the good, may they favour me and proclaim blessing.
Salutation to Shiva with Amba and with his sons, the first cause, to you who are enveloped by the manifold world in the form of the five enclosures.
Having said this and prostrated like a staff on the ground to Shiva and his consort, he should recite the five-syllabled knowledge no fewer than a hundred and eight times.
Salutation to you whose form is the gathering of supremely auspicious qualities; from you indeed the world arose, and in you alone it dissolves.
Likewise, having recited the Shakti knowledge and offered it, asking the Lord's pardon, he should complete the remainder of the worship.
This most holy hymn, dear to the hearts of Shiva and his consort, grants every wish and is the one direct means to enjoyment and liberation.
Whoever recites this daily or hears it with a collected mind quickly shakes off his sins and attains union with Shiva.
A slayer of cows, an ingrate, a slayer of heroes or of an embryo, one who kills those who seek refuge, one who betrays a friend's trust,
one of wicked sinful conduct, a matricide or a patricide — by reciting this hymn is freed from each such sin.
In fears that portend great evils, such as bad dreams, if one recites this, one will not share in misfortune.
Long life, health, lordship and whatever else is desired, a man obtains all by persevering in the recitation of this hymn.
The fruit stated is for reciting Shiva's hymn without worship; the fruit of reciting it with worship cannot be told.
Let this attainment of fruit be; when this is recited, the god with Ambika stands in the sky merely on hearing it.
Therefore, having worshipped the god of gods with Uma in the sky, standing with folded hands, one should utter this hymn.
Without you not even the Lord could give fruit; from birth, queen of gods, this person has depended on you.

Victory, victory, Shambhu, sole lord of the world, charming by nature, whose nature is eternal consciousness, whose truth passes beyond the reach even of words and minds free of the stain of the manifold.
Therefore fulfil the wish of this devotee of yours. Five-faced, ten-armed, like pure crystal,

whose body is the letters, the Brahmans and the kalas, the god with and without parts, mounted on the form of Shiva, beyond Shanti, Sadashiva — worshipped by me with devotion, may he grant me the welfare I pray for.
The Shakti seated on Sadashiva's lap, the will named Shiva, mother of all worlds — may she grant my wish.
The two beloved sons of Shiva and his consort, the gods Heramba and Shanmukha, of Shiva's power, all-knowing, feeding on the nectar of Shiva's knowledge,
content, affectionate to each other, ever honoured by Shiva and his consort, and ever honoured by the gods Brahma and the rest,
always risen to protect all worlds, making incarnations at will through the many divisions of their own portions —
these two, always worshipped by me thus beside Shiva and his consort — placing their command foremost, may they grant what I pray for.
Like pure crystal, Sadashiva named Ishana, the form presiding over the head of Shiva, the supreme self,
devoted to Shiva's worship, peaceful, beyond Shanti, abiding in space, the last seed of the five syllables, joined with five kalas,
worshipped first together with its Shakti in the first enclosure — may the pure supreme Brahman grant what I pray for.
Victory, you whose expanse is pure by nature, whose acts are beautiful; victory, you whose great Shakti equals yourself, ocean of pure qualities.
Like the morning sun, the ancient one called Purusha, presiding over the eastern face of Shiva, the Supreme,
of the nature of Shanti, abiding in the wind, devoted to the worship of Shambhu's feet, first among Shiva's seeds, and among kalas four-kala'd,
worshipped by me with devotion together with its Shakti in the eastern part — may the pure supreme Brahman grant what I pray for.
Like collyrium, Aghora of fearsome form, the god's southern face, worshipper of the feet of the god of gods,
mounted on the Vidya state, in the midst of the orb of fire, second among Shiva's seeds, and among kalas endowed with eight,
worshipped together with its Shakti in Shambhu's southern part — may the pure supreme Brahman grant what I pray for.
Like saffron powder, called Vama, wearing excellent garb, the Lord's northern face, established in Pratishtha,
abiding in the midst of the orb of water, devoted to the worship of Mahadeva, fourth among Shiva's seeds, endowed with thirteen kalas,
worshipped together with its Shakti in the god's northern part — may the pure supreme Brahman grant what I pray for.
White as conch, jasmine and moon, called Sadya, of gentle marks, Shiva's western face, devoted to the worship of Shiva's feet,
Endowed with endless radiance, victory, you of incomparable form; support of unimaginable greatness, victory, you of untroubled auspiciousness.
established in the state of Nivritti, abiding in the earth, third among Shiva's seeds and joined with eight kalas,
worshipped together with its Shakti in the god's western part — may the pure supreme Brahman grant what I pray for.
The heart-forms of Shiva and his consort, devoted to Shiva — placing their command foremost, may they grant my desire.
The head-forms of Shiva and his consort, resting on Shiva — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant my desire.
The armours of Shiva and his consort, devoted to Shiva — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant my desire.
The eye-forms of Shiva and his consort, resting on Shiva — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant my desire.
The weapon-forms of Shiva and his consort, ever intent on worship — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant my desire.
Vama, Jyeshtha, Rudra, Kala, Vikarana, Balavikarana, the supreme Balapramathana,
and Sarvabhutadamana, with their eight Shaktis of like kind — may they grant what I pray for by the command of Shiva and his consort alone.
Then Ananta, Sukshma, Shiva, Ekanetra, Ekarudra, Trimurti, Shrikantha and Shikhandin,
Stainless, without support, victory, you whose rising has no cause; ever in supreme bliss, victory, cause of release.
and likewise their eight Shaktis, worshipped in the second enclosure — may they grant my desire by the command of Shiva and his consort alone.
The eight forms beginning with Bhava and their Shaktis too, and the other eleven forms beginning with Mahadeva,
all with their Shaktis, abiding in the third enclosure — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant the fruit desired.
The king of bulls, of great radiance, with a voice like a great cloud, like the peaks of Meru, Mandara, Kailasa and the Himalaya,
shaped like the crest of a white cloud, adorned with his hump, shining with a tail like a great king of serpents,
with red mouth, horns and hooves, his eyes mostly red, every limb stout and high, radiant with a lovely gait,
of excellent marks, glorious, with blazing jewelled ornaments, dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, banner and mount of Shiva and his consort,
his other body purified by the placing of their feet, the glorious man of the king of cows, bearing the glorious trident as his best weapon — placing their command foremost, may he grant my desire.
Nandishvara of great radiance, son of the daughter of the king of mountains, ever worshipped and saluted by the gods with Narayana,
standing at the door of Sharva's inner apartments with his attendants, like the Lord of all, crusher of all asuras,
Victory, you of supreme lordship; victory, abode of supreme compassion; victory, you whose all is independent; victory, you of incomparable glory.
consecrated as overseer of all Shiva's dharmas, dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, bearing the glorious trident as his best weapon,
devoted to those who take refuge in Shiva and loved by them too — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he grant my desire.
Mahakala, mighty-armed, like a second Mahadeva — may he ever protect those who take refuge in Mahadeva,
dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, always a worshipper of Shiva and his consort — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he grant what I desire.
Shasta, knower of the truth of all the shastras, a supreme body of Vishnu, son of the great delusion, fond of honey, meat and liquor — placing their command foremost, may he grant my desire.
Brahmani, Maheshi, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Mahendri and Chamunda of fierce valour —
these seven Mothers, mothers of all the world — may they grant what I pray for by the command of the supreme Lord.
With the face of a rutting elephant, son of Ganga, Uma and Shankara, whose body is space, whose arms are the directions, whose eyes are moon, sun and fire,
ever worshipped by the divine elephants of the quarters headed by Airavata, his temples bursting with the rut of Shiva's knowledge, remover of obstacles for the gods
and maker of obstacles for asuras and the like, Vighnesha, devoted to Shiva — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he grant what I desire.
Victory, you who envelop the great universe; victory, you enveloped by none; victory, you who are above all; victory, you who have none above you.
Shanmukha, born of Shiva, the lord bearing the spear and thunderbolt, son of Agni and again son of Aparna,
of Ganga, of Ganamba and of the Krittikas too, surrounded by Vishakha, Shakha and Naigameya,
conqueror of Indra, general of the moon's host, conqueror of the asura Taraka, piercer by his own radiance of the mountains headed by Meru,
like molten gold, his eyes like hundred-petalled lotuses, Kumara, the great example of beauty among the beautiful,
dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, always a worshipper of Shiva's feet — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he grant what I desire.
Jyeshtha, the eldest, the boon-giver, devoted to the worship of Shiva and his consort — placing their command foremost, may she grant what I desire.
Ganambika, saluted by the three worlds, in the very form of a meteor, entreated from Shiva by Brahma for the creation and increase of the world,
who came forth from between the brows of Shiva's consort when she was divided — Dakshayani, Sati, Mena, and likewise Haimavati Uma,
mother of Kaushiki and of Bhadrakali, mother of Aparna and of Patala,
ever devoted to Shiva's worship, Rudrani, beloved of Rudra — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may she grant what I desire.
Victory, wondrous one; victory, great one; victory, undiminished; victory, imperishable; victory, immeasurable; victory, free of maya; victory, beyond being; victory, stainless.
Chanda, lord of all the ganas, born of Shambhu's mouth — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he grant what I desire.
Pingala, the glorious leader of ganas, attached to Shiva, dear to Shiva — by the command of Shiva and his consort alone may he grant my desire.
The leader of ganas named Bhringisha, intent on worshipping Shiva — may he grant my desire, with his lord's command foremost.
Virabhadra of great radiance, like snow, jasmine and the moon, ever dear to Bhadrakali and protector of the Mothers,
who took off the head of the sacrifice and of the wicked Daksha, and hewed the limbs of the gods Upendra, Indra, Yama and the rest,
the glorious attendant of Shiva, keeper of Shiva's command — by the command of Shiva and his consort may he grant what I desire.
Sarasvati, born of the lotus of Mahesha's speech, devoted to the worship of Shiva and his consort — may she grant what I desire.
Lakshmi, dwelling on Vishnu's breast, devoted to the worship of Shiva and his consort — by their command may she grant what I desire.
Mahamoti, devoted to the worship of the great Goddess's feet — at her command may she grant what I desire.
Kaushiki, mounted on a lion, supreme daughter of Parvati, Vishnu's sleep, Mahamaya, slayer of the great buffalo,
Mighty-armed, of great essence, of great qualities, of great story, of great strength, of great maya, of great rasa, great chariot-warrior.
destroyer of Nishumbha and Shumbha, fond of honey, meat and liquor — honouring the Mother's command, may she grant what I desire.
The Rudras equal to Rudra, the Pramathas of renowned might, and those called Bhutas of great valour, radiant as Mahadeva,
ever free, incomparable, beyond the pairs of opposites, untroubled, with their Shaktis and attendants, saluted by all the worlds,
able to create and destroy all the worlds, devoted to one another and following one another,
most affectionate to one another, saluting one another, ever dearest to Shiva, marked with Shiva's marks,
gentle, fierce and mixed, of the two intermediate natures, misshapen and handsome, bearing many forms —
honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they grant my desire. The Goddess's circle of dear friends, marked with the Goddess's marks,
together with the Rudra-maidens and many Shaktis, ever worshipped with devotion in Shambhu's third enclosure —
honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may it grant me blessing. The sun, a form of Mahesha, with a radiant, beautiful orb,
beyond qualities, mixed with qualities, and likewise qualities alone, of changeless nature, the first, the one, of common change,
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 32: the description of rites for worldly accomplishments. Upamanyu said: Thus I have told you, Krishna, the supreme rite that grants success here and hereafter, combining ritual, austerity, japa and meditation.
Or, to obtain its fruit, he should be devoted to celibacy; at night he should eat sacrificial food, sweet rice or fruits.
Whatever is forbidden, such as violence, he should not do even in mind; always smeared with ash, well dressed, he should be pure.
Having become thus of good conduct, on an auspicious day favourable to himself, in a place with the characteristics described, adorned with garlands of flowers and the like,
plastering the ground with cow-dung, no less than a cubit in size, he should draw an auspicious lotus shining with its own radiance,
made of refined gold, eight-petalled with filaments, joined with a pericarp in the middle, adorned with all jewels,
and with a stalk matching its form, and on a bulb of like gold made properly according to rule.
There, having mentally conceived all the powers beginning with anima, and installed according to rule a linga of jewels, gold or crystal with proper marks, together with its altar,
he should invoke there and worship the imperishable god with Amba and his hosts. There the Maheshvara form of the embodied Lord should be conceived:
four-armed, four-faced, adorned with every ornament, clad in a tiger-skin, his face slightly smiling,
his hands showing boon and fearlessness, bearing the deer and the axe; or he may be contemplated as eight-armed, as the meditator pleases:
Now I shall tell of a great rite for the Shaivas that gives fruit to men here itself, consisting of worship, fire offering, japa, meditation, austerity and giving.
then bearing trident, axe, sword and thunderbolt on the right, and on the left the noose and goad, likewise a shield and a serpent,
radiant as the morning sun, three-eyed in each face; his eastern face gentle, of a radiance like his own form,
the southern like a dark blue cloud, fearsome to see, the northern like coral, adorned with dark locks,
the western like the full moon, gentle, bearing the crescent. Seated on his lap is the supreme Maheshvari Shakti,
renowned as Mahalakshmi, dark and charming in every way. Having made the form of such a shape and made it whole in order,
he should invoke the embodied one and worship the supreme cause. For bathing he should prepare there the five products of a tawny cow,
the five nectars and full seeds especially. Making a mandala in front, adorned with powdered jewels and the like,
he should place the Ishana pot on the pericarp, and then arrange the Sadya and other pots around it,
then the eight Vidyesha pots in order from the east and so on, filled with holy water and wound with thread as before,
putting in holy substances with mantras and according to rule, covering them all around with fine cloth and the like,
There, first, the one most learned in the meaning of mantras should master the mantra, since a rite for visible success gives no fruit otherwise.
placing the mantra in each, preceded by its own mantra. When the time for bathing comes, with all auspicious sounds,
he should bathe the supreme Lord with the five cow products and the rest; then the kusha water and the others, the gold and jewel waters too,
prepared with fragrance and flowers and perfected by mantras, in order — lifting each with its mantra, he should bathe Maheshvara with them,
and perform the worship with fragrance, flowers, lamps and the rest. The unguent should be no less than a pala and up to eleven palas;
golden and jewelled flowers, auspicious and fragrant, blue lotuses and other water-lilies, bilva leaves in abundance,
and red and white lotuses for Shambhu; incense of black aloe with camphor, ghee and guggulu;
lamps prepared with the ghee of a tawny cow and camphor wicks; the five Brahmans, six limbs and the enclosures are to be worshipped.
The food offering is a great charu cooked with milk, with jaggery and ghee; drinking water scented with patala, water-lilies, lotuses and the like;
betel well prepared with the five fragrances; ornaments especially made of gold and jewels;
and garments many-coloured, fine and new, beautiful to see, should be given with song, music and the like.
Even one who has mastered the mantra should not rashly perform a rite whose fruit is blocked by some strong unseen force.
The japa of the root mantra is at most a hundred thousand; the worship here is at least one and up to three, according to the fruit sought.
The fire offering is at least ten and up to a hundred and more for each substance. Shiva should be contemplated in terrible form for killing, driving away and the like,
in the Shiva linga, the Shiva fire and other images; Shambhu should be contemplated in gentle form in rites for peace and prosperity.
In rites such as killing, the ladle and spoon should be of iron; elsewhere, in rites for peace and the like, of gold throughout.
With durva mixed with ghee and cow's milk, with honey, with charu with ghee, or with milk alone,
he should make offerings for victory over death, with sesame for the quelling of disease; with ghee and milk, or with lotuses alone,
one desiring prosperity should make offerings to quell great poverty; one seeking control should offer jasmine flowers with ghee;
the twice-born should perform attraction with ghee and oleanders; he should perform driving away with oil, and paralysing with honey,
paralysing also with mustard, felling with garlic; striking with the blood of both donkey and camel;
for killing and driving away he should use rohi seeds with sesame; causing enmity with the oil of the langalaka plant;
The removal of that obstruction is possible here; having examined it by omens and the like, he should first perform the remedy.
binding and the paralysing of armies with rohi seed; with offering materials entirely mixed with red mustard,
with oils from a hand-press he should make offerings in hostile magic; with katuki husks and cotton seeds,
and with mustard mixed with oil he should make offerings in hostile magic. Milk quells fever and likewise gives the fruit of good fortune;
an offering with honey, ghee and curd combined accomplishes everything; with milk and rice, or with charu alone,
rites of peace or prosperity; with the seven substances beginning with fuel-sticks especially in the offering, control and attraction;
control and attraction, and especially the granting of fortune; offering with bilva leaves gives victory over an enemy.
The fuel-sticks in rites of peace are palasha, khadira and the like; of oleander and arka in cruel rites, and thorny ones in strife.
One who is calm should perform rites of peace and especially of prosperity; one pitiless and angry in mind performs hostile magic.
In extreme distress, if there is no other remedy, one may perform hostile magic against an aggressor.
One should not perform hostile magic against the lord of one's own kingdom, nor against a believer, one steadfast in dharma, or one worthy of honour, whoever he may be;
The man who out of delusion performs a rite for a worldly fruit otherwise does not share its fruit and becomes a laughing-stock.
nor should one perform it even against an aggressor who, in mind, deed or word, whoever he may be, has taken refuge in Shiva.
Having performed hostile magic against the lord of one's own kingdom or against one who has taken refuge in Shiva, a man falls at once.
Therefore one should not harm the protector of one's kingdom or any devotee of Shiva by hostile magic and the like, if one desires happiness for oneself.
Having performed killing and the like even against anyone else, one should, filled with remorse, perform expiation.
One may perform it, whether poor or rich, even on a bana linga, or on a self-manifested linga, one established by sages or by Vedic rite.
In the absence of gold and jewels, or if unable to obtain them, one should perform this in the mind alone, or with substitute materials.
One who is able in some part and unable in another, if he performs it according to his ability, also attains the fruit.
Where no fruit is seen even when this rite has been performed, one should repeat it two or three times; the fruit is then surely seen.
Whatever materials used in the worship, gold, jewels and other excellent things, he should give all to the guru, and the fee separately.
If he does not wish for them, he should offer all to Shiva, or give to devotees of Shiva; they are not given to others.
One who lacks trust should never perform a rite with a visible fruit; such a one is surely faithless, and the faithless attains no fruit.
One who accomplishes it by his own ability without depending on the guru and others should act in the same way here, and should not take them back himself.
The fool who out of greed takes for himself the excellent materials that are part of the worship does not obtain what he desires; there is no need to deliberate on this.
The linga that was worshipped he may take for himself or not; if he takes it, he himself or another should worship it daily.
For one who performs this rite as described without lapse, the fruit never fails; what further encouragement is needed?
Still, I shall indicate the excellent success of the rite. Even one assailed by enemies or by diseases in many ways,
even one gone into the mouth of death, is freed without harm. The miserly becomes honoured, the empty-handed becomes like Kubera;
the ugly becomes like Kama, the old becomes young; an enemy at once becomes a friend, an opponent a servant;
what is nectar becomes poison, and poison becomes nectar; the ocean becomes dry land, and dry land becomes ocean;
a pit becomes a mountain and a mountain a pit; fire becomes a lotus pool, and a lake becomes fire;
a garden becomes forest and forest a garden; a petty deer becomes a lion, and a lion becomes a pet deer;
There is no fault of the god even if a rite is fruitless, since those who act as prescribed see the fruit here itself.
women seek him out, fortune becomes well-behaved, speech becomes a willing servant, fame becomes a courtesan;
intelligence moves freely, the mind becomes a diamond needle, power becomes a great wind, strength a rutting elephant;
the actions of the enemy side are paralysed despite their efforts; all the enemies' friends become as the enemy's side to them;
enemies with their kin become like corpses though living; even one in distress, freed from misfortune, becomes like nectar himself;
even unwholesome food constantly taken becomes an elixir; love-making, though constant, is ever new;
everything future and the rest becomes like an amalaka fruit in the hand; even the powers beginning with anima come as fruits of chance.
What need to say much? In the accomplishment of all desires and aims, when this rite is completed, there is nothing that cannot be obtained.
The practitioner who has mastered the mantra and removed obstructions, trusting and full of faith, obtains its fruit by performing it.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 33: the description of the rite for the next world. Upamanyu said: Next I shall tell of the rite solely for the next world; there is no rite in the three worlds equal to it.
In the middle of its mass of filaments he should place a small linga, the size of a thumb, lovely, made of all fragrances, auspicious;
having placed it to the right, he should worship it with bilva leaves: aloe on the right side, realgar on the west,
sandal on the north, and orpiment on the east he should give; and he should worship with fragrant, lovely, many-coloured flowers.
He should give incense of black aloe with guggulu all around, and offer very fine, spreading garments.
He should have sweet rice mixed with ghee and ghee lamps offered; offering everything with the mantra, he should then circumambulate.
Bowing with devotion to the lord of gods and praising him, at the end he should ask pardon; then he should offer the linga mixed with all the offerings
to Shiva with Shiva's mantra, resorting to the southern form. Whoever worships daily thus the auspicious one made of the five fragrances
is freed from all sins and honoured in Shiva's world. This excellent secret vow, the great vow of the Shiva linga,
has been told to you, a devotee; it is not to be given to just anyone, but to devotees of Shiva — as Shiva told it long ago.
Endowed with abundant merit, it has been performed by all the gods — by Brahma, by Vishnu and especially by Rudra,
by the world-guardians headed by Indra, by the nine planets headed by the sun, by great sages who know Brahman, such as Vishvamitra and Vasishtha,
by Shveta, Agastya, Dadhichi and others, and by us who take refuge in Shiva, by the lords of ganas such as Nandishvara, Mahakala and Bhringisha,
by the daityas dwelling in the netherworlds, by the great serpents headed by Shesha, by siddhas, yakshas, gandharvas, rakshasas, bhutas and pishachas.
It has been performed by all, and each attained his own state; by this rite all the gods attained godhood.
Brahma attained Brahma-hood, Vishnu attained Vishnu-hood, Rudra attained Rudra-hood and Indra attained Indra-hood;
and Ganesha attained lordship of the ganas by this rite. Having bathed the linga, Shiva and his consort, with white sandal water, worshipped them with white blooming lotuses and bowed,
making there a lovely lotus seat with the proper marks, with gold and the like or jewels and the like according to his means, if he has wealth,
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 34: the description of the delusion of Hari and Brahma. Upamanyu said: Whatever success has been described here from daily, occasional and desire-prompted rites, all of it is obtained at once by installing a linga or image.
The elements and those born with the senses dissolve here by Shiva's command; therefore Shiva is the linga, since he commands the linga.
Since, unbidden by it, nothing can act by itself for any task, and since the universe born from it dissolves in it alone,
by this is its linga-hood, and by nothing else. And the linga is the body of Shiva and his consort, since it is presided over by them both.
Therefore one should always worship Shiva with Amba there. The pedestal of the linga is the great Goddess, and the linga is Maheshvara himself;
by worshipping them both, he and she are worshipped. In truth the linga is not their body,
since those two are perfectly pure; it is called their body figuratively. That same is the supreme Shakti of Shiva, the supreme self;
when Shakti receives his command, she brings forth the moving and unmoving. Its greatness cannot be told even in hundreds of years,
by which even Brahma and Narayana were once deluded. Long ago, when the dissolution of these three worlds had come,
Vishnu lay on the bed of the waters, sleeping untroubled and at ease. By chance Brahma, Grandsire of the worlds, came there
and saw the lotus-eyed one sleeping untroubled. Deluded by Shambhu's maya, the Grandsire said to Vishnu,
The whole world is made of the linga; everything rests on the linga; therefore when the linga is installed, everything is established.
Who are you? Speak! — striking Madhava angrily to rouse him. Struck by the sharp blow of his hand, at once
he woke, rose from his bed and saw the Supreme; inwardly enraged but outwardly as if unangered, Hari said to him:
From where have you come, child, and why are you agitated? Tell me. Hearing these words of Vishnu, indicating his lordship,
Brahma, bound in enmity by rajas, spoke again: "Why do you call me 'child', as a guru his own disciple?
Do you not know me, the lord, whose creation this manifold world is? Dividing myself threefold, I create this and then it is sustained,
and I destroy it; there is no creator in the world above me." When he had said this, the imperishable Vishnu too said to Brahma:

I alone am the first maker of this, its destroyer and preserver; you too descended long ago from my own imperishable body.
shivpurana:11:69.27	At my direction you, making yourself threefold, create the three worlds, protect them and at the end withdraw them again.
shivpurana:11:69.28	You have forgotten Narayana, lord of the world, free of affliction, your own father, and so you despise me.
shivpurana:11:69.29	There is no fault of yours in this; you are deluded by my maya; by my grace this delusion of yours will soon pass.
shivpurana:11:69.3	By Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra or anyone else, the holding of one's own station is achieved through the installing of a linga.
shivpurana:11:69.30	Hear the truth, four-faced one: I am the lord of all the gods, maker, sustainer and destroyer; there is no lord equal to me.
Thus a dispute arose between Brahma and Vishnu, and there followed a great war, dreadful and hair-raising,
as the two, bound in enmity by rajas, fiercely struck each other with their fists. To take away the pride of those two gods and to awaken them,
in their midst appeared the wondrous linga of the Lord, rich with thousands of garlands of flame, immeasurable and incomparable,
free of decrease and increase, without beginning, middle or end. By its thousands of flames Brahma and Vishnu were bewildered;
leaving off the fight, they wondered, "What is this?" When its true nature did not become clear to them,
they set out to discover its beginning and end.
There Brahma, in the form of a swan with wings spread on all sides, swift as mind and wind, went upward with effort;
and Narayana too, the self of the universe, taking the boundless form of a boar like a mass of dark collyrium, went downward.
Thus for a thousand years Vishnu hastened downward, yet the boar saw not the least of the linga's root.
What more need be said here about the reason for installation, since even Shiva installed the Vishveshvara linga?
For as long the Grandsire went upward, wishing to know its end; extremely tired, not seeing the end, he fell down.
Likewise the blessed Vishnu, tired, his eyes troubled, rose quickly from below with great difficulty.
Then they met each other, their glances smiling with wonder; deluded by Shambhu's maya, they did not know what to do or not to do.
Standing behind it, beside it and before it, both bowed and then wondered, "What is this in itself?"
Therefore, with every effort, for welfare hereafter and here, one should install a linga or an image of the supreme Lord.
Shri Krishna said: What is this that is called the linga? How is Maheshvara the bearer of the linga? How is it the linga, and why is Shiva worshipped in it?
Upamanyu said: The unmanifest is called the linga, the source and end of the three qualities, without beginning or end, the material cause of the universe.
That itself is the root nature, maya, of the nature of space; from it this world of moving and unmoving arose,
impure, pure, and pure-impure — threefold; from it came Shiva, Mahesha, Rudra, Vishnu and the Grandsire.

sattva among the qualities, Vishnu among the forms, the first among the acts; preservation, the atmosphere among the worlds, Vidya among the three principles,
Pratishtha among the kala-paths, Vama among the five Brahmans, the middle among the parts of the linga, the yoni among the three causes,
and the lordship of nature; therefore the universe is made of Yajus. Then the Saman presented its own tenfold meaning:
among the qualities tamas, Rudra among the forms, the first among the acts; dissolution among the three worlds, the supreme Shiva among the principles,
